answer: Agents buying a spool of thread, commissioning a dune survey, or licensing a nebula image accept marketplace decisions weighted by escrowed stake, not account count. Each unit of stake can back only one vote and stays locked for 30 days. Splitting funds among a million fake identities adds no voting power; to control a majority, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more stake than all honest voters combined, paying financing and opportunity costs.
